A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Aurora and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B. The additional page in v5 results from reference-list overflow, not missing or added scientific material.

before.justification: v4 reports original acceptance-length and throughput experiments, including day-0 adaptation, synchronization and training-objective studies, and frontier-model evaluations in Sections 4–6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and their results, including the additional throughput measurements in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The asynchronous training–serving architecture, tree attention, acceptance/rejection training objectives, discard sampling, and lazy synchronization procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same mathematical reasoning, SQL, code, finance, and conversational data, with the same mixed-stream, ordered-stream, and held-out evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: The no-speculation and static-drafter controls and the online objective/discard variants remain identical in the corresponding experiments. The newly cited work in Section 2.2 is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 4–6 and Appendix B retain the same request-stream procedures, evaluation metrics, synchronization intervals, lookahead settings, batch sizes, hardware, and training configurations.

E4.justification: The synchronization-frequency, training-objective, discarded-token, top-k, lookahead, and batch-size analyses are all retained without additional or revised evidence.

E5.justification: The existing throughput means and P05/P50/P95 summaries remain unchanged. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The plotted results and numerical entries match, including Figures 3–10 and Tables 1, 4, and 5. For example, Table 1 retains batch-size-1 speedups of 1.57× for MiniMax M2.1 and 1.51× for Qwen3-Coder-Next.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and their associated reasoning are unchanged, including the i.i.d. acceptance approximation, speedup expression, training loss, and memory calculation. No new assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about day-0 deployment, continuous adaptation, serving efficiency, and infrastructure savings. The additional related-work acknowledgment does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations concerning the dominance of online adaptation, conditional benefits of discarded tokens, synchronization tradeoffs, and diminishing throughput benefits at larger batch sizes.

D1.justification: The RPC and buffering details in Appendix A, hardware and optimization information in Appendix B, and disclosed project/model access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 newly acknowledges work combining speculative decoding with online learning and cites Qian et al., When Drafts Evolve: Speculative Decoding Meets Online Learning, as reference 23. The existing comparison with OSD remains unchanged; this is a limited addition to research positioning.

P1.justification: The opening sentences of Section 2.2 are locally revised to accommodate the additional related work. Apart from version/date text and citation renumbering, the language and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Text reflow shifts existing figures vertically, including Figure 6 on page 12, and changes paragraph breaks across pages. The bibliography spills onto a mostly empty extra page. Figure content, axes, legends, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves attribution and contextual completeness by acknowledging a directly related online-learning study in Section 2.2 that v4 omitted. The scientific evidence and technical explanations remain unchanged, and the accompanying layout reflow does not obscure content, so the overall benefit is limited.
